> control, in EVERY branch it can render (loading, empty-catalog, read-only) —

- **(b)** the parenthetical is exhaustive ⇒ the failure arm was **never covered**, which is a **contract gap**, and the fix writes the failure arm into that list first, then implements.

### 3. ⭐ The acceptance discipline, inherited from this family's first card

Triage recorded a failure this lane has already paid for once: objectui#9889's defect was exposed by an assertion the dev then **deleted**. ⇒ this card's acceptance **must** carry an assertion that goes RED on the defect — each failure arm rendered, asserting an accessible name or a `<label for>` that resolves — **and** a still-passing success-arm assertion, or 「fixed」 and 「the check was switched off」 are indistinguishable.

## Seat review — ACCEPT. ⭐ The population was DERIVED, two arms were rejected on the record, and the triage's own suggested fix was proved unavailable.

Seat `domain:ui#2`, `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`, 2026-09-19T04:58Z. Dev report `5739484165`, `status: "done"`, `open_questions: []`. PR objectui#9995, draft.

### 1. ⛔ A correction this seat owes first

My claim comment said 「`PickerLoadFailure` has **ELEVEN call sites**」. Re-derived in this act: the file has 11 **occurrences** = **1 declaration + 10 render sites**. I counted the declaration as a call site. The dev's split is the right one and the number that matters is **10**.

### 2. ⭐ The population was derived, not trusted — which is what the dispatch bought

The dispatch refused the card's list of four and required the in-scope set to come from `WIDGET_LABELLING`. It did, and the result is ⛔ not the card's four:

| site | widget | labelling | in scope? |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `:401` | `ref:object` | control | ⛔ **rejected — already labelable** |
| `:656` | `object-selector` | control | ✅ |
| `:854` | `field-selector` | control | ✅ |
| `:1380` | `field-ref` | control | ✅ |
| `:1457` | `view-ref` | control | ✅ |
| `:2290` | `filter-builder` | control | ⛔ **rejected — already labelable** |
| `:1605` · `:2014` · `:2090` · `:2143` | field-multi, filter-mode ×2, action-multi | **group** | ⛔ out of scope — the named `role=group` container still renders, so the banner only decorates it |

⭐ **Both rejections verified at source by this seat**, ⛔ not taken on the dev's word:
- `:401` — the `PickerLoadFailure` is followed at `:402`–`:403` by `<Input {...controlNaming({ id, ariaLabelledBy })} …>`. The arm already carries a labelable element.
- `:2290` — it renders inside `PopoverContent`, while the labelable `<Button>` in `PopoverTrigger` at `:2286` stays mounted. The `for` resolves.

⇒ the card said four; the derivation says **six `'control'` failure arms, of which four are broken and two were already right**. Rejecting two on the record, **unchanged but still asserted**, is exactly the stop-condition the dispatch wrote — and it is worth more than silently fixing six.

### 3. ⭐⭐ The triage's own suggested repair is UNAVAILABLE, and the dev proved it rather than working around it

Triage offered 「或把 `id` 落到 `PickerLoadFailure` 的容器上并让它成为可标记的」. The dev's finding: `PickerLoadFailure` is a **`div`**, and `for` addresses **only labelable elements**. ⇒ that sub-option cannot be implemented at all. ⛔ Not a preference, a fact about HTML — and it is the kind of thing a dev under pressure quietly substitutes around instead of naming.

The repair instead gives all four the **`ref:object` shape** — an editable freeform anchor carrying `controlNaming` beside the banner — and ⛔ never the `filter-builder` shape. ⭐ And the picker itself is still ⛔ not rendered on those arms, so objectui#5170 and objectui#5227's repair stands untouched: this adds a name, it does ⛔ not resurrect a picker over a failed catalog.

### 4. The fork — reading (a), on four grounds, and the fourth is the strongest

Taken as a **violation**, ⛔ not a contract gap. Its four grounds, in the dev's terms: the docblock calls 「In every branch」 the load-bearing half, so a three-item parenthetical cannot be its meaning; the **membership test the contract actually applies** excludes `field-multi` and `action-multi` for dangling in ONE arm, whichever arm that is; `ref:object` and `filter-builder` were **authored with** the naming on that arm, which under (b) would have been unrequired work; and `PickerLoadFailure`'s own docblock already states the same invariant over that branch.

⭐ The second and third are the ones that decide it: the contract's own applied test and two sites already built to it. The parenthetical is now amended to **name the failed-catalog branch as a record of the settled reading**, with the rule phrase and every widget's declaration ⛔ unchanged.

### 5. Acceptance — the discipline this family paid for once is honoured, and then exceeded

Triage's requirement was a red-on-the-defect assertion plus a still-passing success leg, because objectui#9889's defect was exposed by an assertion the dev then **deleted**. Delivered:

- **RED leg**, from the committed fix by ablation: `Tests 8 failed | 26 passed (34)` — ⭐ exactly the four in-scope arms in **both** layouts (card, via the label's `for`; grid cell, via the column-header IDREF), with the message 「object-selector: the host id is on NO element — the visible label's `for` dangles: expected null not to be null」. Mutation proven by blob hash (`3040ca18a2` → `1056270d40`, `controlNaming` call sites 24 → 20), restore proven by blob equality and an empty `git diff HEAD`, ⛔ never by an exit code;
- **GREEN in the same run**: the success leg over all eleven `'control'` keys with catalogs loaded, and both rejected arms.

⭐ And one guard the dispatch did ⛔ not ask for: an **ARM LEDGER** that reads off the DOM which `PickerLoadFailure` each key actually renders on a failed catalog. ⇒ a widget that stops **entering** its failure arm goes red there **even while the naming assertion goes green**. That closes the hole objectui#9889 fell into from the other side — that pin 「renders loaded catalogs only」, which is why it was green on all eleven while this arm dangled.

⭐ The first test in the file asserts the case table **equals** the `'control'` key set read off `WIDGET_LABELLING` at run time. ⇒ the population cannot drift from the contract without the pin failing. That is a better instrument than any grep this seat ran.

### 6. ⚠️ Two limits declared rather than papered over

- **NOT MEASURED — the parenthetical's chronology.** The dev tried to date the docblock's three-item list against the arrival of the failure arms and found this container's checkout is **shallow** (420 commits, back to 2026-09-11), so `git log -S` resolves both strings to the **shallow-boundary commit** — an artefact, ⛔ not a date. It said so and rested the fork on the text and the code instead. ⭐ Reporting a boundary commit as a date is exactly the trap; naming it is the right move.
- The declared face named `metadata-admin/__tests__/**`, which **did not exist** — the ~40 sibling tests there are flat files. The dev created it, which is literally inside the face and matches `previews/__tests__` and `inspectors/__tests__` next door. ⛔ Not a face breach; noted so the next dev on this family reads the same wording the same way.

### 7. Landing

`check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the three changed paths: **NOT GOVERNED** (the dev's run); this seat re-runs `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr` on the FINAL list before flipping ready.
